tickets.text:
Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync

During the overnight CustomerSync batch window (scheduled 01:00–04:00 PST), the Integration Gateway in us-west-2 began returning repeated 504 Gateway Timeout errors and API call durations exceeding 30 seconds when calling the downstream CRM API endpoint at api.customersync.corplabs.com. This was first reported by Priya Nair (Application Support lead, Portland office) after the Reporting Dashboard failed to refresh overnight customer records. Gateway logs on host INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal showed a token refresh job failure (job ID: tknrot-20251201-0130) in the same time window, indicating the sync process was blocked by downstream authentication issues rather than a general platform outage. Approximately 14,200 customer records were delayed, impacting dependent reporting and sync workflows used by the finance reconciliation team.

input.query: Integration Gateway 504 gateway timeout token refresh job failure
integration gateway service outage escalation application support

steps.result: Engineering, Frankfurt; 0 lockouts in 24 hours; device LT-PRIYANAIR.
No recorded result for integration-gateway-health-check on this ticket.

input.rationale: This is a server-side outage of the Integration Gateway (INTGW-WEST-01, us-west-2) causing 504 timeouts on the CustomerSync CRM API, with a failed token refresh job (tknrot-20251201-0130) in the batch window. The KB has no playbook for this service, and the similar-incident search returned only unrelated access and VPN tickets (s2). The requester's device (LT-PRIYANAIR, image 2026-06, battery 89) and group membership (s4) are healthy and not the cause. The one check I tried for the gateway returned no recorded result (s5), so nothing about the service itself is verified. The failure sits in an internal integration service and its downstream authentication, which belongs to Application Support, not desktop support. It is not something a self-serve or auto-fix path can resolve. Escalating to APP-SUPPORT.
input.summary: Integration Gateway INTGW-WEST-01 (us-west-2) returns 504 timeouts to the CustomerSync CRM API during the 01:00–04:00 PST batch window, after token refresh job tknrot-20251201-0130 failed; about 14,200 customer records are delayed and finance reconciliation is affected.
input.ruled_out: Requester device and account are not the cause: LT-PRIYANAIR is on image 2026-06 with battery health 89, the user has 0 lockouts in 24h, and group membership is normal (s4). The similar-incident search found no matching past ticket (s2). The gateway health check has no recorded result (s5), so platform health and the downstream auth failure remain unverified.
input.next_step: Check the token refresh job tknrot-20251201-0130 and downstream CRM API authentication on INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal, then confirm whether the CustomerSync batch needs a rerun for the roughly 14,200 delayed records.

tickets.text:
Nightly integration timeouts via Integration Gateway (03:00 UTC)

Nightly batch data sync jobs sent through the Integration Gateway to the downstream partner (Acme Data Services) are failing around 03:00 UTC in us-east-1. The gateway returns 504 Gateway Timeout for POST /sync during the scheduled run window, and monitoring shows a matching latency spike at the same time. This is delaying the partner data synchronization workflow for batch-sync-users. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Dallas integration operations team. Current telemetry is incomplete because request correlation IDs and token rotation history were not available in the original evidence. The affected API client ID is intg-client-batch-7741, and the integration service account username is svc_batchsync. Requests originate from host WORKSTATION-INTGOPS-MD (10.42.18.97).

input.query: Integration Gateway 504 Gateway Timeout batch sync partner

steps.result: Sales, Portland; 0 lockouts in 24 hours; device LT-MDELGADO.

input.rationale: The query describes 504 Gateway Timeout on POST /sync during the 03:00 UTC batch window, with a matching latency spike, affecting the Acme Data Services partner sync. Retrieval returned no matching playbook (s1 empty), and similar-incident lookup (s2) returned only unrelated Outlook/Software Center tickets. The requester record (s3) shows Sales, Portland, LT-MDELGADO, not an integration-ops host; the reported origin WORKSTATION-INTGOPS-MD (10.42.18.97) and service account svc_batchsync are not in this requester's directory record, and the reporter is named as Dallas integration operations. This is a gateway/integration service-side timeout involving a service account and API client, which is beyond desktop support scope and cannot be resolved with a documented fix. Escalating to the network/application queue that owns the gateway path.
input.summary: Nightly POST /sync batch jobs from intg-client-batch-7741 (svc_batchsync, host 10.42.18.97) return 504 Gateway Timeout at ~03:00 UTC in us-east-1 with matching latency spike, delaying Acme Data Services partner sync.
input.ruled_out: No KB playbook matched (s1). Similar-incident search (s2) returned only unrelated Outlook and Software Center tickets, so no prior precedent applies. Requester account has 0 lockouts in 24h and no recent tickets (s3), and the device LT-MDELGADO is healthy (2026-06 image, battery 98%), so the desktop and account side are not the cause. Token rotation history and correlation IDs are missing, so credential expiry and gateway-side timeout are not yet ruled out.
input.next_step: Pull Integration Gateway logs and correlation IDs for POST /sync between 02:45 and 03:30 UTC in us-east-1 for client intg-client-batch-7741, and check upstream Acme Data Services response latency and the svc_batchsync token rotation history.

tickets.text:
Integration Gateway API timeouts causing PaymentSync failures

PaymentSync backfill and scheduled synchronization jobs intermittently failed between 02:10 and 02:40 UTC on 2025-12-08 when the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-east-07.payments.internal) timed out while calling the downstream payment API endpoint at https://api.payments.internal/v2/sync. This caused queued sync work on the paymentsync-worker pods in the us-east-1 Kubernetes cluster, delayed payment data updates for Finance Users, and repeated 504 timeout responses logged by the gateway. The issue was initially reported by Rajesh Menon (rmenon@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office after the PaymentSyncApp dashboard showed stalled jobs. Immediate recovery was observed after token rotation by ops engineer Lisa Cheng, but available validation evidence did not show token expiry, so the incident is best explained as downstream latency with token rotation treated as a coincidental or non-causal mitigation.

input.query: PaymentSync Integration Gateway timeout downstream latency
payment gateway downstream latency escalation queue

steps.result: Sales, Munich; 0 lockouts in 24 hours; device LT-RMENON.

input.rationale:
The issue is a server-side payment integration failure: PaymentSync jobs timing out at Integration Gateway gateway-prod-east-07 calling api.payments.internal, with 504s logged by the gateway, on the us-east-1 Kubernetes cluster. Knowledge base searches returned no matching playbook and no similar closed incidents (all results had near-zero similarity), so no documented cause or fix applies. The requester record (rmenon, Sales, Munich, Dell Latitude 5440, 2026-06 image, 0 lockouts) shows a normal desktop profile, so the endpoint is not the source; the fault lies in backend infrastructure and the payments API. The reported token rotation had no proven causal link. This falls under infrastructure ownership beyond desktop support, so it cannot be self-served or auto-fixed. Escalating to the app team that owns the integration, with a P2 priority because Finance payment data updates are delayed.</rationale>
<parameter name="cause">Unknown
input.summary: PaymentSync backfill and scheduled jobs timed out (504) between 02:10 and 02:40 UTC on 2025-12-08 when gateway-prod-east-07 called https://api.payments.internal/v2/sync, delaying Finance payment data updates; the likely cause is downstream API latency, and token rotation by Lisa Cheng is not shown to be causal.
input.ruled_out: Requester endpoint: the device LT-RMENON is healthy (2026-06 image, 0 years old, 85% battery, 0 lockouts in 24h), and no account issue applies. Token expiry: not shown by the available validation evidence. No KB playbook or similar closed incident matched, so no documented fix applies.
input.next_step: Review gateway-prod-east-07 and api.payments.internal latency and 504 logs for 02:10–02:40 UTC on 2025-12-08, and confirm with the payments/integration owner whether the downstream endpoint was degraded and whether the token rotation had any effect.

tickets.text:
Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service behind Load Balancer

Internal users and dependent services were trying to reach the svc-internal endpoint (svc-internal.corplabs.internal) over TLS through the load balancer LB-EAST-02, but clients began showing certificate warnings and rejecting the connection. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, who noticed that requests from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MC were returning NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID errors. The load balancer presented an expired certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal, expired 2025-12-10T00:00:00Z) and an incomplete chain after the renewal window was missed, which blocked normal access to the internal web service and caused TLS handshake failures for internal integrations in us-east-1. Multiple teams including the payroll integration service (contact: David Ortiz, emp ID E-40291) confirmed downstream failures.

input.query: load balancer expired TLS certificate renewal svc-internal
expired TLS certificate load balancer internal web service
server certificate renewal load balancer escalation queue

steps.result: Engineering, Frankfurt; 0 lockouts in 24 hours; device LT-MARIACHEN.

input.rationale: The ticket describes an expired server-side TLS certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal, expired 2025-12-10) and an incomplete chain on load balancer LB-EAST-02, affecting many internal clients and downstream services (payroll integration). This is not a user-side device problem: the requester's device LT-MARIACHEN (HP EliteBook 840, image 2026-06, age 0 years, battery health 70, no lockouts) is healthy and the fault sits on the load balancer's certificate. None of the retrieved VPN playbook content applies, and the device-certificate reset tool would not fix a server certificate on the load balancer. The KB search found no runbook for load balancer certificate renewal. Per the escalation-queue reference, the owner is the team that runs the failing system: APP-SUPPORT owns internal services and their certificates. Priority is raised to P2-High because multiple teams and integrations are down.
input.ruled_out:
User device LT-MARIACHEN is current (image 2026-06, age 0 years) with 0 lockouts, so the client side is not the cause. The VPN device-certificate playbook does not apply because the expired certificate is on the server load balancer, not the endpoint. No similar closed incident matched a load balancer certificate renewal; the similar incidents found were about Wi-Fi RADIUS and endpoint VPN certificates.</ruled_out>
<parameter name="queue">APP-SUPPORT
input.summary: Load balancer LB-EAST-02 is presenting an expired certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal, expired 2025-12-10T00:00:00Z) with an incomplete chain, causing TLS failures for internal clients and downstream integrations including payroll.
input.next_step: Renew the svc-internal.corplabs.internal certificate on LB-EAST-02, install the full intermediate chain, and verify the TLS handshake from us-east-1 and from the payroll integration service (contact David Ortiz, E-40291).

tickets.text:
Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage

Users and internal integrations were trying to access the Internal Web Service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com through the load balancer (LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal), but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and dependent API calls from services owned by the Platform Engineering team failed TLS negotiation. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40291) from the Denver office at approximately 02:05 UTC on 2025-12-17. The service became unavailable over TLS after the presented certificate (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com, issued by CorpLabs Internal CA) passed its validity window on 2025-12-16T23:59:59Z, and the load balancer continued serving an outdated certificate chain containing an expired intermediate, blocking normal internal application access for all users in the us-east-1 environment.

input.query: expired TLS certificate internal web service load balancer outage
expired TLS certificate load balancer ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID
certificate renewal load balancer intermediate chain escalation

input.rationale: The query describes an expired TLS certificate and expired intermediate chain on load balancer LB-EAST-02 serving portal.internal.corplabs.com for all us-east-1 users. The requester record (maria.chen, Frankfurt, device LT-MARIACHEN) shows the reporter is a single engineer, so this is not a device-side issue. Searches returned no playbook for load balancer certificate management, and the similar incidents (INC-WCI-0016, INC-WCI-0006) show expired server certificates fixed by renewing them with a full chain on the server, which is infrastructure work. No remediation tool applies to a load balancer certificate, so this must go to the network/infrastructure team. Path is ESCALATE to NET-DNS? No: the closest owner for load balancer and network infrastructure is NET-DNS for name/endpoint issues, but the certificate renewal on a load balancer is network infrastructure, so NET-WIFI does not apply either. Routing to NET-VPN is also wrong. The best match is the infrastructure team that owns the load balancer, which the available queue list maps to NET-DNS for hostname and endpoint services. Priority is P1 because it blocks internal access for all users in us-east-1 and dependent Platform Engineering APIs.
input.summary: Load balancer LB-EAST-02 is serving an expired certificate and expired intermediate for portal.internal.corplabs.com, causing TLS failures for all us-east-1 users and Platform Engineering APIs.
input.ruled_out: Device-side causes are ruled out: the requester's device LT-MARIACHEN is on the 2026-06 image and the outage is reported across all users, so it is server-side. No matching KB playbook was found (search s1 and s3 returned nothing), and similar incidents only cover wireless controller certificates, not load balancer chains.
input.next_step: Renew the certificate for portal.internal.corplabs.com on LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal with the valid CorpLabs Internal CA chain, replacing the expired intermediate, and verify TLS handshakes succeed.

tickets.text:
Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage

Internal developers on the Platform Engineering team were trying to access the internal API at https://internal.example.corp/v2/services over HTTPS, but browsers began showing certificate warnings and automated clients (including CI/CD pipelines running on WORKSTATION-BUILD-MK) started failing TLS handshakes at approximately 07:15 UTC on 2025-12-20. The affected endpoint was internal.example.corp behind load balancer LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp, which made the internal web service unreachable over TLS and blocked normal API calls for the entire Arlington development group. Monitoring did not alert before the outage — the certificate-management-service renewal job configured by r.navarro had not fired its 30-day pre-expiry notification. Renewal response was delayed until developer Priya Chandrasekaran (emp ID EMP-40821) reported the issue and the expired certificate being served by the load balancer was confirmed by the infrastructure team.

input.query: expired TLS certificate internal web service outage
expired TLS certificate load balancer internal service
certificate expiry load balancer renewal APP-SUPPORT

steps.result: fail: The certificate presented for internal.example.corp (serial 4A:7C:9E:02:BB:31) was expired as of 2025-12-20T07:15Z, matching the reported start…

input.rationale: The issue is an expired TLS certificate presented by the load balancer LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp for internal.example.corp, not a user-side problem. Check cert-expiry-check (s4) failed: the certificate (serial 4A:7C:9E:02:BB:31) expired at 2025-12-20T07:15Z, matching the reported start of the outage, and the CN matches the endpoint. The KB has no playbook article for this failure (s1, s3 returned nothing), and the similar incidents are device or Wi-Fi certificates, not server-side service certificates. The failing system is an internal web service and its certificate, so it belongs to APP-SUPPORT, not the reporting team. Renewal requires the infrastructure side, which is beyond desktop support scope.
input.summary: Expired certificate on load balancer LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp for internal.example.corp (serial 4A:7C:9E:02:BB:31, expired 2025-12-20T07:15Z) is blocking TLS for the Arlington/Platform Engineering development group and CI/CD on WORKSTATION-BUILD-MK.
input.ruled_out: Certificate expiry confirmed by cert-expiry-check (s4): the served certificate is expired and its hostname matches, so the cause is server-side, not the requester's device or profile. No matching playbook article was found (s1, s3). Similar device and Wi-Fi certificate incidents (s2) concern client-side certificates, not this server certificate.
input.next_step: Renew and deploy a valid certificate for internal.example.corp on LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp, then verify the TLS handshake from WORKSTATION-BUILD-MK, and check why the certificate-management-service 30-day renewal notification for r.navarro did not fire.
